W-001.name: Alder Bench Cellars
W-001.note: A big, buttery Napa Chardonnay that coats the glass: toast and butter first, then a squeeze of lemon. Impressive, but at this price I wanted more freshness. Better with roast chicken than on its own.

W-004.name: Alder Ranch Wines Ridge Selection
W-004.note: Lean and tidy: pear, a little vanilla from the oak, then a clean finish. I poured it with prawns at a barbecue and the bottle was gone before the grill was hot.

W-005.name: Azienda Agricola Camposcuro
W-005.note: Cherry jam and almond skin, with a slightly raisiny sweetness in the middle. A cosy winter wine; I had it with a very average lasagne and it made the lasagne better.

W-007.name: Azienda Agricola Poggiofiorito Campo Grande
W-007.note: The 2019: dusty cherry, dried thyme and a tomato-leaf edge, tannins still a bit firm. Needs food, ideally pasta with a proper tomato sauce.

W-008.name: Azienda Agricola Poggiofiorito Campo Grande
W-008.note: The 2020 is the friendlier sibling: ripe cherry, plum and softer tannins, and cheaper than the 2019. Surprisingly, I liked it more. Pizza night wine.

W-010.name: Azienda Agricola Sassodorato
W-010.note: Smoky and salty, like licking a warm rock on a volcano island (I haven't, but I imagine this is it). A whiff of smoke, lemon peel and flint, bone dry with sharp acidity. Expensive, and only worth it with seafood.

W-011.name: Azienda Agricola Villanuovo Colle Lungo
W-011.note: Dark chocolate, prune and a bitter-cherry finish that goes on and on. Big but not clumsy. A wine for a long dinner and a slow conversation; I would not serve it with anything lighter than beef.

W-013.name: Bluestem Ranch Wine Co.
W-013.note: Pale salmon colour, strawberry and a hint of rose petal. Pretty, light and dangerously easy to drink on a balcony. A little pricey for a rosé.

W-015.name: Bluestem Ridge Vineyards Single Vineyard
W-015.note: Silky and a bit mysterious: black cherry, a little clove, a wisp of smoke, then a long mineral finish. This is the Pinot I would pour for someone who says they don't like red wine.

W-018.name: Bluestem Terrace Cellars Estate Selection
W-018.note: Blackcurrant, cedar and a polished tobacco note; huge structure and tannins you could chew. Beautiful, but it is a €300 bottle and it knows it. Needs another five years.

W-028.name: Bodega Valle Nueva Block 12
W-028.note: Plum and blackberry with a bit of vanilla, no complications, and under nine euros. My go-to weeknight red for steak or burgers.

W-031.name: Bodega Vega Nueva
W-031.note: Light-bodied and juicy: raspberry, a touch of violet and a snap of pepper at the end. Twenty minutes in the fridge and it was perfect with tapas.

W-033.name: Bodegas Cumbre Nueva Tierra Alta
W-033.note: Apple, lemon and fresh bread, bone dry, with bubbles that tickle. At under ten euros it is my new party default.

W-036.name: Bodegas Valle Alta
W-036.note: Classic Rioja: vanilla and cedar over dried cherry, soft tannins after its years in barrel. Tastes the way my grandfather's cellar smelled.

W-039.name: Cantina Collechiaro
W-039.note: Green apple, pear and a hint of sweetness, with soft, gentle bubbles. A lovely aperitif, though not for people who like their sparkling bone dry.

W-042.name: Cantina Mondorato
W-042.note: Toast and brioche, yellow peach and a creamy mousse. This is what I wish more Champagne tasted like at this price.

W-046.name: Cantina Valsereno
W-046.note: Jammy! Prune, blackberry and a sweet liquorice finish. Big and warm, like a hug from a slightly overbearing uncle. Fine for a barbecue, too heavy for a hot evening.

W-050.name: Cascina Fontebruno
W-050.note: Peach, orange blossom and grape juice with the tiniest fizz. Sweet and light; I had it with a fruit tart on a Sunday. Not a wine for serious people, and that is fine.

W-052.name: Cascina Monscuro Bricco Rosso
W-052.note: Rose petals, tar and cherry; the tannins grip hard, so decant it. Had it with mushroom risotto and it was one of those 'oh, now I get Nebbiolo' evenings.

W-056.name: Château Belereau L'Ancienne
W-056.note: Dried apricot, orange peel and honey, with enough acidity to keep it from turning syrupy. Pour a small glass with blue cheese and then enjoy the silence.

W-057.name: Château Beleval
W-057.note: Black pepper, thyme and blackberry with grippy, leathery tannins. Big Mourvèdre energy; I would give it three more years and a lamb shoulder.

W-059.name: Château Fontancourt
W-059.note: Cedar and blackcurrant with a pencil-shaving dryness; austere right now, the kind of wine that makes you sit up straight. Good, not lovable.

W-062.name: Château Lauvereau
W-062.note: Plush plum and chocolate, rounder than the Médoc wines I tried that week. Low on acidity, easy to love and a bit forgettable.

W-063.name: Château Lauveval Terroir d'Argile
W-063.note: Cut grass and grapefruit from the Sauvignon, honeysuckle and a waxy note from the Sémillon. Sophisticated, a little oily in texture, worth the money.

W-066.name: Château Montancourt Les Silex
W-066.note: Blackcurrant, violet and a whisper of cedar; full-bodied but graceful. I would serve it blind against a Napa Cabernet and bet it wins.

W-072.name: Château Rouvaval
W-072.note: Chewy tannins and the oak is still loud: tar and smoke on top of dark fruit. Too young. I am keeping the second bottle until 2030 and will report back.

W-074.name: Château Tarvault Les Silex
W-074.note: Pear, almond and a slightly oily, off-dry texture. Rich but soft; I liked it with a creamy chicken dish.

W-075.name: Château Valmardent Cuvée Prestige
W-075.note: Very pale pink, strawberry and a little thyme, crisp and dry. The bottle looks expensive; the wine is just very good.

W-078.name: Château Vaucancourt Les Grands Champs
W-078.note: The 2018 is firm but friendly: blackcurrant and a pinch of cedar for under twenty euros. A very honest Bordeaux.

W-082.name: Château Vermaval Clos du Moulin
W-082.note: Gooseberry, cut grass and wet stones, with razor-sharp acidity. Goat cheese, a green salad, done.

W-087.name: Domaine Aubaie-Pernellac Terroir d'Argile
W-087.note: The 2022 has more weight than the 2023: lemon, a bit of butter and an oyster-shell salinity. Very Chablis. A bit pricey, but better balanced.

W-088.name: Domaine Aubaie-Pernellac Terroir d'Argile
W-088.note: The 2023 is leaner and sharper: green apple, lemon and a clean mineral edge. Cheaper, and I enjoyed it a little less on its own, but it is excellent with oysters.

W-089.name: Domaine Boscobello Estate Selection
W-089.note: Sour cherry, dried tomato and tobacco, with tannins like a firm handshake. Greek and very unusual; I would pour it with lamb and say nothing until someone asks what it is.

W-090.name: Domaine Brunancourt-Querault
W-090.note: Apple, pear and toast from a little oak, with more weight than a plain Chablis. Beautiful, but at over a hundred euros I would drink the village wine and buy a second bottle.

W-092.name: Domaine d'Ormeval Terroir d'Argile
W-092.note: Pepper, smoke and thyme from the hills (so the label says; I mostly taste barbecue). For six and a half euros it is hard to beat, rustic and chewy.

W-094.name: Domaine de Brunouze
W-094.note: Apple and honeysuckle with a firm line of acidity, and none of the sugar I was expecting. Dry Vouvray is underrated; this one was beautiful with roast chicken.

W-095.name: Domaine de Clerouvre
W-095.note: Lime, green apple and a touch of flint, bone dry and very focused. Sushi and this: yes.

W-104.name: Domaine de Malvereau Cuvée Charlotte
W-104.note: A slightly green bell pepper note on top, then cedar and tobacco; I wanted more fruit for €78. Elegant but dry-edged. I am leaving this one to my dad.

W-107.name: Domaine de Rochouvre L'Ancienne
W-107.note: Pretty cherry and raspberry with mouthwatering acidity, a rosé that behaves like a white. Charming, but €53 for a rosé needs a justification I could not find.

W-116.name: Domaine de Vermouvre Cuvée Tradition
W-116.note: Apple, almond and a creamy mousse, dry but never harsh. Drank it with a cheese tart and felt like I was in Colmar.

W-117.name: Domaine des Aubépines
W-117.note: Pear, hazelnut and orange blossom, round and a little waxy; a rare white you want slightly warmer than fridge temperature. Too expensive for a Tuesday.

W-119.name: Domaine des Coteaux Dorés
W-119.note: Hazelnut and apple with a savoury, sherry-like note that I am told is a Jura thing. Not for everyone: I loved it and my partner did not. Try it with a hard cheese.

W-121.name: Domaine des Genêts L'Ancienne
W-121.note: Almond, apple and honeysuckle, dry and dense with a bitter edge. It needed a second glass to make sense. Roast pork helped.

W-122.name: Domaine des Grands Champs Les Silex
W-122.note: The 2019: raspberry, liquorice and a warm finish with black pepper; powerful but smooth. A solid choice for the Sunday lamb.

W-123.name: Domaine des Grands Champs Les Silex
W-123.note: The 2020 has the same house style but is darker: plum, smoke and a thread of liquorice. More concentrated and tighter, and I preferred the 2019, which was easier to drink now.

W-126.name: Domaine des Terrasses La Source
W-126.note: Banana-and-strawberry juice in the best sense: very fresh, very soft, almost no tannin. Serve it slightly cool with charcuterie.

W-127.name: Domaine Dorvault-Brunaval Les Terrasses
W-127.note: Peach, a little butter and toast; ripe, round and polished. Safe but good, especially with a creamy pasta.

W-129.name: Domaine Estraval-Valmardent Cuvée Prestige
W-129.note: Raspberry, clove and violet, with the kind of silky texture you remember a week later. Expensive, and I would buy it again. The dinner-party wine that makes people go quiet.

W-131.name: Domaine Fontellac-Vaucelle
W-131.note: Cherry and clove with a savoury, forest-floor note; tighter and more tannic than I expected from Pinot. Needs time. I opened it too early and I am still a bit annoyed with myself.

W-136.name: Domaine Malvelle-Lancancourt Clos du Moulin
W-136.note: Apple, lemon and a little vanilla; round, easy and uncomplicated. A good everyday Chardonnay for a roast chicken.

W-139.name: Domaine Querereau-Valmeval Les Hauts Plans
W-139.note: Cherry and raspberry with a bit of smoke; more powerful than the 1er Crus I tried. Honest and structured, but 89 euros is a lot for a village wine.

W-155.name: Fattoria Boscochiaro Vigna del Nonno
W-155.note: Apple, pear and toast, very dry and lean. A serious sparkling wine that needs shellfish; on its own a little austere.

W-157.name: Fattoria Poggiobello Vigna Alta
W-157.note: Almost transparent pink, cherry and a whiff of almond; light, soft and summery. Great value, and I finished it before the pasta arrived.

W-159.name: Finca Cumbre Alta Finca Vieja
W-159.note: Raspberry, strawberry and vanilla with a spicy pepper edge; fruity, friendly and a little simple. Tapas wine.

W-169.name: Foxglove Ranch Vineyards
W-169.note: Cherry, raspberry and clove; a little tannic for a Pinot but pleasant. Great with salmon or duck.

W-172.name: Granite Run Vineyards Old Vine
W-172.note: Bell pepper and cedar over tobacco, which I did not expect from California at this price; very firm tannins. Interesting, not generous.

W-177.name: Larkspur Fork Estate Ridge Selection
W-177.note: Peach and a little raspberry, clean acidity, tiny bubbles. English fizz is no joke; I would serve it before a Champagne and nobody would guess.

W-178.name: Larkspur Ridge Estate Single Vineyard
W-178.note: Plum, blackberry and smoke, big tannins, bold. Barbecue wine, or wine for people who like their wine loud.

W-181.name: Maison Dorvignac
W-181.note: Blackberry, black pepper and violet. Powerful, tight and extremely young; after decanting it opens into something almost floral. Worth waiting for.

W-183.name: Maison Estraval Terroir d'Argile
W-183.note: Cherry, raspberry and a lick of violet; a bit more structure than the other Morgon I tried. Fresh and lovely with roast chicken.

W-185.name: Maison Jourdeval Blanc de Blancs
W-185.note: Apple, butter and toast, with a very fine mousse; elegant, taut and long. Great with oysters, but expensive for a non-vintage.

W-188.name: Maison Lauvonne Blanc de Blancs
W-188.note: Peach, pear and butter, rounder and softer than the Jourdeval. Less tension but more fun, and twenty euros cheaper.

W-194.name: Maison Tarvouvre Cuvée Tradition
W-194.note: Apple, raspberry and a chalky dryness; very crisp, rather severe. Good, but €98 for a non-vintage that wants food is a tough sell.

W-196.name: Maison Vermereau Cuvée Tradition
W-196.note: Pear, peach and toast with a creamy, almost nutty depth; the 2014 shows what bottle age does for Champagne. A birthday wine.

W-198.name: Meadow Bench Vineyard Hillside Block
W-198.note: Blackberry, pepper and liquorice; thick, warm and generous, and the cheapest way to impress a steak lover.

W-200.name: Poderi Boscodorato Colle Lungo
W-200.note: Plum and cherry with a rustic pepper snap. Pizza wine, nothing more, nothing less, for nine euros.

W-204.name: Poderi Collescuro
W-204.note: Cedar, plum and pepper; polished, hugely expensive, and I could not tell it from a good Bordeaux blind. That is probably the point.

W-207.name: Poderi Villanuovo
W-207.note: Lemon, almond and a hint of fennel; crisp and slightly bitter at the end in a pleasant way. My risotto wine, no questions.

W-208.name: Quinta da Cabeço Sereno Lote 7
W-208.note: Lime, green apple and a faint spritz; super light and refreshing. Nice with sushi, forgettable on its own.

W-220.name: Tenuta Monchiaro Campo Grande
W-220.note: Cherry, rose and tar, with grippy tannins. A Barolo at 35 euros already sounds suspicious, but it works. Cook mushrooms with it.

W-222.name: Tenuta Roccalungo
W-222.note: Lemon, green apple and an almond finish; clean, crisp, very easy. I would drink this with a risotto and not think twice.

W-224.name: Tenuta Vallungo Vigna Alta
W-224.note: Grapefruit, lemon and fennel with a salty note, as if bottled at the beach. Grilled fish, obviously.

W-240.name: Weingut Hanghof
W-240.note: Peach, green apple and a gentle sweetness in a very light body. Wonderful with spicy food; the acidity cuts right through. A summer wine, even in winter.

W-243.name: Weingut Moselhalde Steillage
W-243.note: Lime and lemon with a flint edge and slightly sweet fruit; more intense than the Hanghof but also pricier. Excellent with curry.

W-249.name: Weingut Sonnental Terrassen
W-249.note: Grapefruit and white pepper, and the pepper is the signature. Nice with vegetables and pork, and good value.
